title: rasterized-prefix-replayer-and-sparse-telemetry-compressor
author: Maya Patel
body: Motivation: Large-scale session replays for multi-model benchmark runs produce very large trace volumes that slow both storage and replay pipelines. This PR implements two complementary systems to reduce footprint and speed up deterministic replays: (1) Rasterized Prefix Replayer (RPR) that groups similar token prefixes into raster keys to deduplicate warmup and common prompt fragments; (2) Sparse Telemetry Compressor (STC) which converts dense per-token telemetry into sparse, event-driven encodings with configurable windowing. Deliverables: rpr/runner (deterministic rasterized replayer), stc/compressor (streaming compressor with CLI and bindings), bench/integration harness and baseline report, migration scripts for S3 archives, docs and runbook. Results: on a representative multi-model workload (mixed sequence lengths, heterogeneous batch sizes) we observed a 2.1x median reduction in stored trace size, a 9% improvement in ingest throughput at p95, and ~12% reduction in full-session replay time for long sessions; fidelity regressions on prompt-preserving overlap metrics were <0.3% (within tolerance). Backwards compatibility: decompressor included; runtime toggle via BENCH_RPR_ENABLED environment variable and config flags for rasterization resolution. Rollout: nightly alpha in benchmark-lab for two weeks, then incremental migration of historical archives one shard at a time. Risks: rasterization collisions (mitigated by salted hashing and monitored collision counters); transient memory spikes in streaming compressor (mitigated via windowed flush and backpressure). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for compressor library; - [x] deterministic replay unit/integration tests; - [x] benchmark job definitions and raw outputs; - [x] migration script for archived traces; - [x] docs (design doc + runbook); - [x] Grafana panels and dashboard updates.
commits: Initial prototype of rasterized prefix replayer (rpr/runner) with deterministic ordering and seedable hashing
Add streaming sparse telemetry compressor (stc) and CLI with protobuf framing and RLE encoder
Integration harness: bench/integration/rpr_endtoend.py and synthetic workload generator
S3 migration helper scripts and unit tests for compressed object verification
Docs: design doc, runbook, and troubleshooting section for collisions and memory tuning
Fix: bound compressor memory and add windowed flush to avoid OOM on long sessions
Perf: small micro-optimizations to prefix hashing and buffer reuse to lower latency
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice direction — can you quantify how rasterization granularity affects fidelity? Please add a small ablation in the benchmark harness.
Maya Patel (reply): Added a param sweep in bench/integration that records ngram-overlap at three granularities; results are in bench/results/rpr_granularity.csv
Priya Rao: We should avoid implicit global state in the compressor that could leak between runs. Move the window config into explicit contexts.
Maya Patel (reply): Addressed — compressor now takes an explicit CompressorContext and is safe for reuse in long-running processes. Added tests to assert no cross-run state.
Diego Martinez: CI flagged flakiness in test_rpr_determinism on low-entropy seeds. Please ensure seeding is deterministic across platforms.
Maya Patel (reply): Switched to a portable hashing primitive and added cross-platform seed compatibility tests. Re-ran CI; flakiness resolved.
ci_checks: performance-suite: pass (baseline comparisons attached in bench/results)
merge_details: Merged by Priya Rao via squash merge on 2026-03-02; merge_commit: a1b2c3d4e5f6
release_notes: Introduce Rasterized Prefix Replayer and Sparse Telemetry Compressor to reduce benchmark trace storage and speed deterministic replays. Includes migration tooling and dashboards. Toggle with BENCH_RPR_ENABLED.
notes_for_ops: When enabling on production archival jobs, run migration on a single shard and monitor rpr.collision_count and stc.window_memory_bytes. If collision_count increases unexpectedly, roll back and inspect salts/config. Use provided decompress CLI for read-path compatibility.
